pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Thallium Toxicity (Poisoning) THE SMOKING GUN: The classic toxic triad of severe, painful ascending peripheral neuropathy, acute neuropsychiatric symptoms/psychosis, and delayed dramatic alopecia (hair loss). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium (Tl+) acts as a biological cellular toxin due to its ionic radius being nearly identical to Potassium (K+). It readily substitutes for potassium in crucial physiological processes, interfering with the Na+/K+-ATPase pump and cellular energy production in the mitochondria. It also cross-links intracellular protein sulfhydryl groups, disrupting keratin synthesis. This results in severe axonal degeneration (causing painful sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy and autonomic instability), central nervous system toxicity (causing confusion, psychosis, and seizures), and rapid disruption of hair follicle matrix cells leading to anagen effluvium (alopecia).
